claims.claim: At the advertised knight-encounter staging configuration, the idealized ambiguous move has the two global possibilities ±r, and both stated branches are exclusive and end in K(q+r;a,r,f).
claims.evidence: Fixing the orthogonal colored-neighbor and wall directions leaves exactly the identity and reflection in their span; their orbit on the remaining signed unit direction is {r,−r}. Exact enumeration over all 48 signed orthogonal bases confirms every stated move is unit or idle, every round has distinct destinations and no edge swap, and both branches reach {q+r,q+r+a,q+3r+f}=K(q+r;a,r,f). This verifies only the stated idealized positional macro.
claims.witness: The −r branch reaches the target after two rounds. The +r branch passes through H=q+r+f and reaches the same target after three rounds.
claims.search_method: Independent symbolic reconstruction followed by exhaustive integer enumeration of all 48 signed-coordinate frames.

claims.claim: From the advertised ordinary-transition staging configuration, the distinct-choice branch gives D(q;d,e,f), while the contact-and-rotation branch gives D(q;e,d,f), without a collision or edge swap.
claims.evidence: From {q,q+d,q+f}, moving the third robot by e gives {q,q+d,q+e+f}=D(q;d,e,f). Alternatively, contact at q+d+f followed by q→q+e and q+d→q gives {q,q+e,q+d+f}=D(q;e,d,f). Orthogonality of d,e,f makes all moves unit or idle; exhaustive checking finds neither coincident destinations nor reverse traversal of one edge.
claims.search_method: Exact vector arithmetic for both choices (d,e)=(a,−r),(−r,a), enumerated over all signed orthogonal bases.

claims.claim: From the advertised outer-reset conversion staging configuration, every choice of d, x and the ±d conversion branch is exclusive and ends in K(s;y,d,x).
claims.evidence: For each d∈{a,−r}, x∈{e,−f}, and conversion sign, the correction produces {s,s+x,s+2d+x}. The final simultaneous moves s→s+y and s+x→s yield {s,s+y,s+2d+x}=K(s;y,d,x). Exhaustive exact checking confirms unit-or-idle displacements, distinct destinations, and no edge swap in every round.
claims.witness: In the +d branch M corrects to s+x; in the −d branch M corrects to s+2d+x while C occupies s+x. Both then undergo the same final positional transfer.
claims.search_method: Enumerated all choices of signed orthogonal a,r,f, both d/e assignments, both x/y assignments, and both conversion signs.

claims.claim: The three retained positional macros do not define or prove a visibility-one algorithm with at most 76 shades.
claims.evidence: The source defines an algorithm as (Cl,Init,T) and requires every permitted execution from every allowed initialization to perpetually explore every eligible cave. The macros provide no shade set, initialization map, total local-view transition function, compatibility proof, reachability/composition invariant, or global coverage proof. Their coordinate correctness therefore cannot establish the construction alternative.
claims.witness: No Cl with |Cl|≤76, Init, or total T appears anywhere in the draft.
claims.search_method: Compared every supplied construction component against the source’s formal algorithm and PEP definitions.

claims.claim: If a visibility-one algorithm for exactly three Batdroids without common chirality solves PEP, then on every N×N×N cave with even N≥14, every permitted execution has infinitely many rounds in which some Batdroid's current rule admits more than one global destination.
claims.evidence: Assume an execution has an all-unambiguous suffix. At its start, choose an empty center, possible because an even cube has more than three centers. PEP forces a first later entry. The entrant cannot have been lost immediately beforehand, since a non-idle lost move has six possible global directions, so another robot was adjacent. The source’s exhaustive adjacency cases then apply using only unambiguity along this realized suffix: a connected triple is trapped in a central slice; a pair containing the entrant is confined to a center-crossing line until central-slice contact; an isolated entrant remains at the center while the nearby pair is line-confined; and three isolated robots become permanently idle. Every case contradicts PEP. Thus no execution has an ambiguity-free suffix.
claims.witness: The contradiction uses the four exhaustive three-robot adjacency types at the first post-suffix center visit: connected path, entrant-pair plus isolate, isolated entrant plus pair, or three isolates.
claims.search_method: Re-derived the suffix-local contradiction from the source’s visibility-one symmetries, distance bounds, PEP quantifiers, and center-case proof.

claims.claim: The recurrent-ambiguity obstruction is shade-blind and does not provide a lower bound separating 76 shades from 77.
claims.evidence: The obstruction quantifies over arbitrary robot shades and uses only positions, walls, visibility-one symmetries, and destinations. It proves recurrent ambiguity is necessary but excludes no positive shade-set size. Consequently it cannot distinguish 76 shades from 77.
claims.witness: The argument remains unchanged when Cl is replaced by any nonempty shade set.
claims.search_method: Dependency audit of every step in the recurrent-ambiguity proof against the source model.

claims.claim: Neither alternative in the target is established.
claims.evidence: The draft supplies neither a complete algorithm tuple using at most 76 shades with a universal PEP proof nor an impossibility theorem excluding every such algorithm. The positional macros and shade-blind necessary condition do not fill either gap.
claims.witness: The construction alternative lacks Cl, Init, T, and global correctness; the optimality alternative lacks any shade-count lower bound.
claims.search_method: Direct target-coverage comparison against both alternatives in the exact source target.

target_evidence: The recurrent-ambiguity theorem is a correct, nontrivial necessary condition on every candidate solution, and the three conditional positional macros are arithmetically correct. This is valid partial progress. It does not resolve the target because it neither constructs a visibility-one PEP algorithm with at most 76 shades nor proves that all such algorithms are impossible. The parent explicitly claims only PARTIAL resolution, so that characterization is accurate.
